questions.question: Whose job is #32, and which JTBD does it trace to?

options.label: New job, Robin extended (Recommended)
options.description: Register a new job — operate a forge without learning its hazards by contact — under the existing persona robin-backlog-curator. The outcome is distinct from keep-a-backlog-trustworthy (that one is about what a card MEANS; this is about whether the instance constants are known before they bite), but the human is the same one who owns the board, so no new persona is minted.

options.label: New facet of keep-a-backlog-trustworthy
options.description: No new job. Record #32 as a setup facet of Robin's existing job, on the card's own argument that the payoff is groom-issues rule 4 no longer going dark. Cheapest in SSOT churn; risks burying the forge-hazard outcome inside a backlog-hygiene job that never mentions it.

options.label: New job AND new persona
options.description: The actor is an adopter standing the plugin up on a repo's board for the first time — arguably not Robin, whose mental model is entirely about card meaning. Most faithful to the card's 'the point is the next repo', at the cost of a ninth persona very close to an existing one.

questions.question: What is the provisional driving surface? (DESIGN confirms; DISCUSS needs an entry point for the elevator pitches)

options.label: New command (Recommended)
options.description: A new /phil:* command that owns probe-and-write, e.g. /phil:board-setup. Clean single responsibility, re-runnable, and nothing else has to grow a mode. Adds a command to the surface area.

options.label: Add a path to /phil:groom-issues
options.description: Grooming already reads the whole board and already reports rule 4 unevaluated — so it is the command that DETECTS the missing declaration. Folding setup in means the detector can fix what it found; risks making a report-only command a writer, which its own journey forbids.

options.label: New command + an invariant check
options.description: The command writes the block; a scripts/ check (this repo's stated mechanism-for-a-convention rule) fails when a repo has board work but no declaration. Most in line with CLAUDE.md's 'a convention with no enforcement'; largest slice count.

questions.question: UX research depth for the journey?

options.label: Comprehensive (Recommended)
options.description: Full journey with emotional arc, shared-artifact registry and error-path map — matching groom-issues and single-issue-per-feature. The error paths are where this feature's value is (a stale option ID, a declaration that disagrees with the labels in use), so they want real mapping.

options.label: Lightweight
options.description: Happy path only: probe, elicit, write. Fastest to DESIGN; the fixtures the card demands (stale section, disagreeing declaration) would then be specified without a mapped failure mode behind them.

options.label: Deep-dive
options.description: Multiple personas and extensive edge cases — adopter, curator, and a repo where a teammate already hand-wrote half the block. Likely overkill for a single-surface command.

options.label: Yes — thin end-to-end slice 01 (Recommended)
options.description: Slice 01 probes one real board and writes a block into a repo with no ## Issue board section at all, end to end, and gets dogfooded the same day. It disproves the central bet — that the probeable half is actually probeable — before any elicitation work is built on top of it.

options.label: No — feature is isolated enough
options.description: Go straight to the full slice split without a skeleton, on the grounds that this repo authors prose and the risk is low. Loses the early disproof of the probe assumption.
